lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Other receivables
lines.why: Owed by suppliers and others, not by customers (vendor non-trade receivables): operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Revenues from Advanced Technology Solutions in 2025 were $1.2 billion, representing 23.7% of our 2025 net revenues.
Revenues from Core Business Services in 2025 were $3.9 billion, representing 76.3% of our 2025 net revenues.
Data-Tech-AI revenues in 2025 we r e $2.5 billion, representing 48.1% of our 2025 net revenues.
Digital Operations revenues in 2025 were $2.6 billion, representing 51.9% of our 2025 net revenues.
Revenues from our Financial Services segment in 2025 were $1.4 billion, representing 26.7% of our 2025 net revenues.
Revenues from our Consumer and Healthcare segment in 2025 were $1.7 billion, representing 34.0% of our 2025 net revenues.
Revenues from our High Tech and Manufacturing segment in 2025 were $2.0 billion, representing 39.3% of our 2025 net revenues.
In 2025, 71% of our revenues were derived from clients based in North America and 22% of our revenues were derived from clients based in Europe.
No single customer accounted for more than 10% of the Company's consolidated net revenues in 2023, 2024 or 2025.

• Our success largely depends on our ability to develop and achieve our business strategies, and our results of operations and financial condition may suffer if we are unable to continually develop and successfully execute our business strategies.
Our future growth, profitability and cash flows largely depend upon our ability to continually develop and successfully execute our business strategies.

Our industry relies on large numbers of skilled employees, and our success and profitability depend on our ability to attract, train and retain a sufficient number of employees with the right mix of skills and experience, including advanced technology skills, to deliver our services and solutions to our clients.

Our clients, suppliers, subcontractors, and other third parties with whom we do business, including in particular cloud service providers and software vendors, generally face similar or greater cybersecurity threats, and we must rely on the safeguards adopted by these third parties.

We and our clients rely on third-party cloud, software, and open-source components, and vulnerabilities or failures in those supply chains (including “zero-day” exploits) may introduce or amplify risk, trigger client and regulatory claims, and increase remediation costs.

Our competitiveness also depends on our ability to continue to develop and implement services and solutions that anticipate and respond to rapid and continuing changes in technology to serve the evolving needs of our clients.
Certain aspects of the Labor Code rely on the issuance of rules and regulations.

Our revenue and profitability depend on the demand for our services and solutions with favorable margins, which could be negatively affected by numerous factors, many of which are beyond our control and unrelated to our work product.

Our operations depend on our ability to anticipate and quickly address our and our clients' needs for products and services, as well as our suppliers’ ability to deliver the required products and services at reasonable prices and in time for us to meet our own client commitments.

Our ability to generate revenue from these arrangements will depend on our partners’ or other third parties’ desire and ability to successfully perform the functions assigned to them in these arrangements.
The successful execution of our growth strategy also depends on our ability to effectively manage and develop our strategic partnerships and alliances.

Our ability to effectively offer a wide range of business solutions depends on our ability to attract existing or new clients to new service offerings, and the market for our solutions is highly competitive.

A portion of our business depends on the ability of our employees to obtain the necessary visas and work or entry permits to travel to and do business in the countries where our clients and, in some cases, our delivery centers, are located.
Any decision to do so will depend on the condition of the capital markets and our financial condition at such time.
Our business depends on our ability to successfully obtain payment from our clients of the amounts they owe us for work performed.
Our success also depends on our ability to develop and protect intellectual property rights in our AI-enabled solutions, including proprietary AI models, algorithms, and methodologies.

In order to protect our rights in these various intellectual properties, we rely upon a combination of nondisclosure and other contractual arrangements as well as patent, trade secret, copyright and trademark laws.

Any determination to pay dividends to holders of our common shares in the future, including future payment of a regular quarterly cash dividend, will be at the discretion of our board of directors and will depend on many factors, including our financial condition, results of operations, general business conditions, statutory requirements under Bermuda law and any other factors our board of directors deems relevant.
Due to its inherent limitations, including that it relies on sample-based testing, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements.
The ultimate realization of deferred tax assets depends on the generation of future taxable income during the periods in which temporary differences are deductible.
